sources.entry: Writing - Lightweight distraction-free text editor, in the browser (Markdown and LaTeX supported). No lag when writing. (Source Code) MIT Javascript

summary.one_liner: Writing is a lightweight, distraction-free Markdown and LaTeX text editor that runs in the browser with no server.
summary.what_it_does: The editor runs as a static page: opening index.html is the whole installation, and the README says no server code is needed so it can run offline. It supports Markdown with LaTeX/MathJax math formulas, rendered as you type with the author stating there is no delay or flicker. Keyboard shortcuts toggle a display mode (CTRL+D), open the print or save-as-PDF dialog (CTRL+P), and save the source as a .MD file (CTRL+S). A help panel (CTRL+SHIFT+H or the ? icon) lists other commands such as changing the font. The README describes the interface as deliberately minimal, with no welcome or login page.
use_cases: write Markdown documents in a browser
edit text with LaTeX math formulas
how_to_run: Open index.html in a web browser
notable: No server or installation needed; works offline from index.html
Renders Markdown with LaTeX/MathJax math without typing delay or flicker
Minimal interface: write, preview, save, print or export to PDF
Landing page is the working page, with no welcome or login screen
caveats: Some bundled libraries were modified slightly, so they are shipped in the package rather than used as stock upstream versions
The README mentions no paid tiers or platform limits; feature scope is intentionally small
